label: Publish
tagline: Take a prototype live on the internet using the user's own GitHub + Supabase
description: Publishes a Woven prototype to a real public URL using the USER'S OWN accounts (never Woven's). API / GitHub-app first: creates a GitHub repo under the signed-in account, exports the prototype source, pushes, enables a static host (GitHub Pages for the MVP), and returns the live URL. When the app stores data, it provisions a Supabase database whose schema is DERIVED from the prototype's OWN entities + IA (prototype.json), not a hardcoded template, confirms that schema with the user, then wires the screens to real reads/writes so clicking around actually persists, and redeploys. Detects whether GitHub is linked and, if not, emits a link-GitHub task instead of failing. Lets the user pick a domain target (default github.io / a free getwoven.design subdomain / their own custom domain) and a how the agent works: AUTOMATIC (API, cheapest, server-side), AI BROWSER-USE (drives provider dashboards, most tokens), or WORK TOGETHER (the agent gives click-by-click steps and the user performs each one, the safe user-driven path). No separate dry-run flag - safety is the plan-then-confirm in AUTOMATIC / AI BROWSER-USE and the user-drives nature of WORK TOGETHER. Detects existing state (already-connected repo / prior publish.json) and updates rather than duplicating. The DB schema + role-scoped RLS are read from the data model Woven already has (prototype.json entities + links / arrows), so the database matches the actual app; still deferred: a standalone complex-app classifier + the two-agent grill loop. Writes durable state to <project>/publish.json (the seed of the development-task surface). Honors the no-terminal-for-user rule: in AUTOMATIC the agent does the work; in GUIDED it hands the user click-by-click steps, and only because they chose it.

triggers.title: publish / deploy / take it live
triggers.rule: User wants the current prototype put online (publish, deploy, ship it, take it live, put it on the internet, give me a real URL, host it). Dispatch publish-orchestrator. It gates on GitHub being linked, detects whether the project was already published (and updates rather than duplicating), honors the chosen way it works (automatic API / browser-use / work-together) + domain target, runs M1 (static deploy) and, when the app stores data, M2 (a real Supabase database whose schema is derived from the prototype's own entities, with the screens wired to real reads/writes). It uses the USER'S accounts via the stored GitHub token + a Supabase token the user connects - never Woven's infra.

hardRule.body: When the user asks to PUBLISH / DEPLOY / take a prototype live / put it on the internet / get a real shareable URL that is NOT the ephemeral getwoven.design share tunnel, dispatch the `publish-orchestrator` (Task subagent_type: publish-orchestrator). Do NOT attempt the GitHub repo creation, push, host enablement, or Supabase provisioning inline yourself - the orchestrator owns the cost-warning, the way it works (automatic API / browser-use / work-together), the domain target, the GitHub-linked + existing-state detection, and the durable publish.json state machine. Publishing uses the USER'S OWN GitHub + Supabase accounts, never Woven's broker/tunnel infra (that is only for previews).
